entities.name: PMID:10752813
observations: In 22 postoperative ventilator-dependent adults with acute lung injury, baseline RAP predicted cardiac-index change during 15-second apneic airway-pressure increases to 30 cmH2O (r²=0.68). RAP ≤10 mmHg identified a larger cardiac-index fall (30%±9% vs 8%±7% for RAP >10 mmHg; p<0.01).

entities.name: PMID:10710387
observations: In 10 anesthetized patients, apneic positive airway pressure of 15 cmH2O increased RAP from 7.3±3.1 to 10.0±2.3 mmHg and reduced left-ventricular stroke volume by 23%±22%; baseline RAP prediction was not tested.

entities.name: RAP predicts PAP response
observations: In acute lung injury, lower baseline RAP predicts greater cardiac-index deterioration during brief apneic positive airway pressure; RAP was a stronger predictor than PAOP or RV EDVI in the reported study.
